text: Two ways to protect the rows of a CRM Analytics dataset: borrow Salesforce's own sharing rules, or write a filter yourself. Most real designs use both. Here's how to choose.

Sharing inheritance lets a dataset built from a Salesforce object apply that object's sharing logic to its rows. Defaults, role hierarchy, and sharing rules you already built carry over, so a user sees the rows they could see in Salesforce. When an admin changes a rule, analytics follows. It's accurate, and it spares you from hand-coding role hierarchies as predicates.

But it has limits. A dataset inherits from one Salesforce object, even if it was built from several. And inheritance can't always be honored, for example when a user's access exceeds documented limits. Salesforce guidance says to also set a security predicate as a fallback. Exact limits change by release, so check the current documentation, and remember that inheritance says nothing about warehouse data.

A custom predicate fits when data isn't from Salesforce, when the rule is a business rule like reps seeing their own region, or when you want a rule auditors can simply read. The cost is upkeep, since nothing reminds you when territories change. Here's a fallback shown for illustration. Keep it strict, verify the syntax, and document which datasets use which approach.
Simple choice: one Salesforce object, inherit and add a fallback. External data or business rules, write a predicate. Next up: Governance for Enterprise Analytics.
